subject: Enterprise performance assay: load resilience & measurement approach
messages:
From: Sophie Clark <sophie.clark@stratton.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Subject: RFP section: performance measurements - clarification

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this. We're compiling the performance annex for the Stratton RFP and need a concise description of how Redwood will demonstrate: steady-state throughput, tail-latency behavior at production concurrency, cold-start characteristics, and graceful degradation during resource contention.

Specific asks:
- Do you provide a reproducible harness we can run (or observe) that replays a representative traffic trace?
- How do you define steady-state vs warmup for multi-replica setups?
- Can you provide expected p50/p95/p99 latencies for an 8k-token context, 128-token output (rough order of magnitude) and the measurement methodology?
- What are the quantization/model-variant knobs you will test and how do you report quality vs cost tradeoffs?

We prefer concrete measurement steps (tooling, metrics, datasets) rather than high-level claims. If you have a short plan we can include in the RFP response, please send it back by COB Monday so procurement can review.

Appreciate it — Sophie
Stratton Financial (RFP lead)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: RFP section: performance measurements - clarification

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear asks. Below is a concise, reproducible "assay" we propose you include in the RFP. I've attached a short PDF with the same steps plus example scripts and a small sample workload file for review (performance-assay-plan.pdf; workload-samples.jsonl).

Executive summary (one paragraph you can paste):
Redwood will execute a controlled, reproducible load resilience assay that measures steady-state throughput, tail-latency composition, cold-start profiles, and graceful degradation across model variants and quantization levels. The assay combines real-traffic replay (timing-preserving), synthetic burst sweeps, and soak tests; results are reported as per-request latencies (p50/p95/p99), tokens/sec, cache hit-rate, error-rate, and cost-per-1000-tokens for each model/hardware configuration.

Planned methodology (step-by-step):
1) Test harness and reproducibility
   - We provide a Dockerized harness (Prometheus + Jaeger + load generator) and a recorded trace replayer that preserves inter-arrival timings and session grouping. You can run it in your lab or we can run it in Redwood's dedicated test tenancy and share raw metrics.

2) Workload definition
   - Canonical set: 5k session-based prompts, mix of short (<=32 tokens) and long (up to 8k context) prompts, output targets 16–256 tokens. We will include an anonymized sample corpus (see workload-samples.jsonl).

3) Warmup vs steady-state
   - Warmup period: 10 minutes of gradual ramp to target concurrency (to populate KV/cache and JIT paths). Steady-state window: subsequent 30 minutes used for primary metrics. For long-run soak tests we run 6–24 hours.

4) Metrics captured
   - Latency (per-request): total, prompt-encode, model-forward, generation-per-token; reported p50/p90/p95/p99/p999.
   - Throughput: requests/sec and tokens/sec; effective throughput vs concurrency.
   - Cache/KV hit-rate: prefix-cache hits and effective token savings.
   - Error types: OOM, timeouts, 5xx, model-fallback occurrences.
   - Cost: estimated infra $/1k tokens for the observed profile.

5) Scaling sweeps and graceful degradation
   - Horizontal sweep: increase concurrent sessions in steps while holding QPS per-session constant.
   - Vertical sweep: vary batch sizes and model quantization (fp16, int8/4-bit where supported).
   - Fallback policy validation: verify automatic fallback to smaller model variant or lower-precision path under constrained capacity and record degradation in latency/quality.

6) Cold-start characterization
   - Measure cold-start latency distribution by cycling replicas (stop/start) and recording first N requests post-start. Report p50/p95/p99 for first request and for the first minute of traffic.

7) Quality vs cost reporting
   - For each config (model+quantization+hw), we report BLEU/ROUGE-like task metrics or task-specific scoring on a small eval set, together with cost and latency curves to enable tradeoff decisions.

Instrumentation and evidence
- Exported metrics: Prometheus metric names and labels, Jaeger traces, and raw request/response logs (anonymized).
- We will provide Grafana dashboards and a CSV of aggregated results.

Test matrix (examples)
- Model variants: open-llama-7b / 13b; quantization: fp16, int8; hw: A10G-equivalent, A100-80GB, H100.
- Concurrency envelope: 10–200 simultaneous user sessions; per-session QPS 0.1–2.0.

Deliverables and timeline
- Draft assay results (lab run in Redwood tenancy): 5 business days from access approval.
- On-site witness run or tenant run: additional 3–5 business days as needed.

Notes & caveats
- Performance numbers vary by prompt length, model architecture, and tokenization. The assay focuses on apples-to-apples comparisons (same corpus, same warmup).
- If you need independent verification, we can coordinate a joint lab run with Stratton engineers present or provide sanitized raw traces for your own replay.

Next steps
- Confirm whether you want Redwood to run the primary assay in our test tenancy or prefer a guest-run (we'll share the Docker harness either way).
- If guest-run, provide a short network allowance window and (optionally) a service account for access.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer

Karthik / Sophie — quick clarifying points from procurement:
- We want at least one numeric example in the RFP text so reviewers have context. Can you include a "typical observed" ballpark for p95/p99 for a 512-token context, 64-token response on an A100-equivalent machine? Even a range is fine.
- Is the harness able to preserve session stickiness for multi-request conversations? We need to ensure caching behavior is realistic.
- For the guest-run option, what logs/retention do you need? Stratton's security team will want to limit retention to 30 days and ensure PII stripping.

Also: can you list the rollback criteria for a canary that would trigger failover to the previous deployment (e.g., p99 > X ms for Y minutes, error-rate > Z%)?

Thanks — Ethan
Stratton Financial (procurement)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cross <ethan.cross@stratton.com>, Sophie Clark <sophie.clark@stratton.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T11:45:00-05:00
Subject: Re: RFP section: performance measurements - clarification

Ethan — thanks, good points. Short answers and an example paragraph you can paste into the RFP: 

Numeric example (illustrative; RFP will state ranges and caveats):
- For a 512-token context and 64-token generation on an A100-80GB class node, typical observed results in our lab runs (with warmup) are: p50 ~ 70–120 ms, p95 ~ 240–380 ms, p99 ~ 520–900 ms for single-replica, non-batched synchronous requests. With batching and throughput-optimized config, tokens/sec can exceed 4k–6k depending on model size and batch policy.

Session stickiness and caching
- The harness preserves session affinity (same session id across related requests). That allows realistic prefix-cache behavior and per-session KV cache hits to be measured. We report cache hit-rate and show the effective reduction in model-forward time when prefix cache is exercised.

Guest-run retention and PII
- For guest-run we ask for a short-lived service account and a temporary S3 (or equivalent) bucket. We will strip PII at ingress (simple redaction heuristics documented in the attached instrumentation checklist). Redwood can be configured to retain logs for the requested 30-day window and then securely delete archives; we will include a signed attestation for that process if needed.

Canary rollback criteria (example thresholds)
- Automatic rollback triggers we recommend:
  • p99 latency breach: p99 > 2x baseline for >= 10 minutes
  • Error-rate: 5xx rate > 0.5% for >= 5 minutes
  • Successful request ratio: < 98% for >= 10 minutes
If any trigger fires, the system initiates a canary failover and notifies engineering + CS. Those thresholds are configurable by account and can be tightened for production SLAs.

If this is acceptable I'll (a) attach a 1-paragraph numeric example with caveats to the RFP draft and (b) schedule a lab run for next week.

Cheers,
Karthik
Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
